question:
A survey was conducted on the patients who have undergone knee replacement surgeries. It was found that, Robotic Knee replacement surgeries have 90% success rate. On a particular day, robotic surgery was performed on three patients, A, B and C, one after the other. Assuming that the success and failure of each surgery is independent of each other, find the probability that :
(i) exactly one surgery is successful,
(ii) at most two surgeries are successful.
explanation:
(i)

Step 1 Identify the parameters for the binomial probability distribution. Let a successful surgery be a "success". The probability of success for a single trial is $p = 90\% = 0.9$. The probability of failure is $q = 1 - 0.9 = 0.1$. The number of independent trials (patients) is $n = 3$.

Step 2 State the formula for the binomial probability mass function: $P(X=k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k q^{n-k}$, where $X$ is the random variable representing the number of successful surgeries.

Step 3 To find the probability of exactly one successful surgery, evaluate the formula at $k=1$. Substitute the parameters to get $P(X=1) = \binom{3}{1} (0.9)^1 (0.1)^2$. This equals $3 \times 0.9 \times 0.01 = 0.027$.

(ii)

Step 4 To determine the probability of "at most two" successful surgeries, we want $P(X \le 2)$. This can be calculated directly by adding $P(X=0) + P(X=1) + P(X=2)$, but it is computationally simpler to use the complement rule: $P(X \le 2) = 1 - P(X=3)$.

Step 5 Calculate the probability of exactly three successes. Substituting $k=3$ into the binomial formula yields $P(X=3) = \binom{3}{3} (0.9)^3 (0.1)^0 = 1 \times 0.729 \times 1 = 0.729$. Using the complement rule, $P(X \le 2) = 1 - 0.729 = 0.271$.
